title: AI Needs Trusted Journalism
gist: Teaser-length piece: Stig Ørskov argues that AI chatbots siphoning news traffic and profits have broken the publisher–tech bargain (journalism in exchange for discovery), and proposes UNESCO's draft Guidance on Fair Compensation for News as a basis for a new value-exchange model.

themes.theme: AI chatbots break the publisher-platform bargain

insights.claim: The traditional bargain in which publishers funded journalism while tech firms helped audiences discover it is no longer workable as people increasingly rely on AI chatbots for news.
insights.speaker: STIG ØRSKOV
insights.so_what: Signals rising pressure for AI firms to pay for news content, a potential cost line for AI model operators.
insights.quote: the already tenuous bargain between publishers and tech firms—the former invested in journalism that the latter helped audiences discover—is no longer workable
insights.locator: As people increasingly rely on AI

insights.claim: AI chatbots are siphoning traffic and profits from news outlets, many of which already operate on shoestring budgets, putting good journalism at risk of disappearing.
insights.speaker: STIG ØRSKOV
insights.so_what: Referral-traffic erosion threatens ad- and subscription-driven media business models.
insights.quote: siphoning traffic and profits from outlets often operating on a shoestring budget, good journalism is at risk of disappearing

insights.claim: UNESCO's proposed Guidance on Fair Compensation for News could serve as the basis for a new value-exchange model between news publishers and AI/tech companies.
insights.speaker: STIG ØRSKOV
entities: Guidance on Fair Compensation for News
insights.so_what: A multilateral compensation standard could translate into licensing fees or regulation affecting AI companies' content costs.
insights.quote: UNESCO’s proposed Guidance on Fair Compensation for News could help create a new value-exchange model.
insights.locator: As people increasingly rely on AI

insights.claim: Trustworthy journalism is an indispensable source of the agreed factual information without which, following Hannah Arendt, freedom of opinion is a farce and democracies cannot function effectively.
insights.speaker: STIG ØRSKOV
insights.so_what: Frames news compensation as a democracy issue, strengthening the political case for intervention against AI platforms.
insights.quote: Freedom of opinion is a farce unless factual information is guaranteed and the facts themselves are not in dispute.

top_entities: Guidance on Fair Compensation for News
